text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P1 created — single-AZ VPC peering route flap detected affecting us-east-1a inference fleet. Symptoms: gRPC stream resets (RST_STREAM), increased 5xxs, kv-cache regen. Pager -> oncall. Link: http://ops/incident/3344447777

maria (oncall): seeing ~18% 5xx on model-pool-us-east-1a, tail latencies >2s. Pages firing. Starting mitigation steps now.

kevin (sre): quick triage: repeated route withdraws in peering route table, resolver timeouts. gRPC errors show ECONNRESET and RST_STREAM. kv-cache miss rate spiking to 45%. Sample log: 
```
2024-10-12T14:31:22Z ERROR grpc: stream reset: code=2, err=RST_STREAM
2024-10-12T14:31:23Z WARN kvcache: miss burst for shard-7, regen start
```

sajal (infra): aws console: peering connection pcx-0abcd showing route list flapping — route propagations intermittently removed for prefix 10.20.0.0/16 -> controlplane. Opened AWS support case 1234567890. No instance termination events.

beth (support): customers CUST-42 and CUST-99 reported elevated errors (retries, 502). Drafting status update to customers now.

maria (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) Redispatch inference traffic away from us-east-1a to warm pool in us-east-2, 2) throttle ephemeral concurrency on us-east-1a to reduce kv-cache regen, 3) enable additional client-side retry/backoff where safe.

kevin (sre): I can run the reroute. Dry-run first: `rbctl reroute --from us-east-1a --to us-east-2 --percent 30 --dry-run` then apply. Also will add a short delay on proxy reconnects to reduce thundering.

deploy-bot: dry-run OK — predicted shift: 28-32% traffic to us-east-2, no config drift detected.

maria (oncall): applying reroute now (+30% to us-east-2). Monitoring metrics.

maria (oncall): t+2m: 5xx down from 18% -> 7%, kv-cache miss rate -> 22%. Latency tail improving.

kevin (sre): pushed proxy backoff change (conn retry jitter 200-800ms) and lowered ephemeral concurrency on us-east-1a nodepool via `k scale` to 60% of baseline.

beth (support): sending customer note: "We're investigating an infrastructure networking issue in us-east-1a impacting streaming inference. We've shifted most traffic to a healthy region and are monitoring. Will update in 30m." :email:

sajal (infra): AWS responded: they see repeated route withdrawals likely tied to ENI rescheduling in the peering path. Their provisional suggestion: recreate the peering route propagation and monitor; that requires careful maintenance to avoid controlplane disruption.

maria (oncall): keeping redispatch live. Current split: us-east-2 45%, us-east-1a 55% (we increased after seeing improved perf). 5xx now ~1.6%. Continuing to monitor for peering stability.

kevin (sre): plan: keep failover active until AWS confirms stable route propagation or we perform controlled maintenance. Will prepare post-incident RCA and map which shards saw highest kv-cache churn.

maria (oncall): oncall handoff in 30m to kevin. I'll update postmortem stub and customer comms.

incident-bot: Incident 3344447777 status -> monitoring. Pager cleared to oncall.

kevin (sre): handoff acked. I'll own night monitor and follow up with infra to schedule peering repair with minimal customer impact. Adding action item: reduce automatic kv-cache regen threshold for us-east-1a to avoid cascade on flaps.

beth (support): customers notified, no major escalations after reroute. I'll keep CS loop open. :thumbsup:

kevin (sre): final note before shift: keep traffic split and watch for resolver TTL spikes; if 5xx >3% for 10m, escalate back to P1. Will add to incident timeline.

maria (oncall): thanks team — handing off.
